To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) IDMs can present with CHI; (2) KCNJ11-associated CHI can present with severe hypoglycemic episodes; (3) HNF4A -CHI can present with a clinical phenotype different from that previously described in the medical literature.
we report 2 infants of diabetic mothers that were diagnosed with congenital hyperinsulism.
we describe two IDMs with CHI due to a rare pathogenic KCJ11 and HNF4a gene variants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diagnosis of rare forms of CHI in infants of diabetic mothers and the need for genetic testing in these infants to confirm the diagnosis.
the clinical presentation, genetic etiology, and treatment of two infants of diabetic mother (IDMs) with congenital hyperinsulism.
the identification of rare genetic variants in two IDMs with CHI and their clinical phenotypes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CHI can occur in IDMs, and that the clinical presentation can be quite different than that of non-IDMs.
CHI should be suspected as the etiology for hypoglycemic infants born from mothers with gestational and/or type 2 diabetes.
CHI should be considered as a differential diagnosis in all cases of persistent hypoglcemia in IDMs and should be ruled out with a genetic test.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IDMs are more prone to develop CHI than the general population and that CHI in IDMS may present with a different clinical phenotype.
IDMs are not exempt from CHI, and that HNF4A-related CHI has a variable phenotype.
CHI should always be considered and ruled out in IDMs with persistent hypoglycemias.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CHI can be challenging to diagnose, and that IDMs are not exempt from this condition.
the clinical presentation of HNF4A CHI may be quite different than previously reported, and that IDMs should always be considered a possible etiology of CHI.
CHI should be suspected in IDMs who present with persistent hypoglycaemia, even if the hypoglycaemic episodes are not associated with ketosis or acidosis.
